title: command palette performance monitor missing 2 icon after last update

judgment.rationale: The missing GPU and Network icons correspond to the latest Command Palette dock organization change rather than an identified rendering failure. A maintainer explained that the performance monitor widgets were decoupled and can be restored through Edit Dock; the current provider code creates separate GPU and Network dock bands with their expected icons.
evidence: The reporter clarified that the missing icons are GPU and Network and that they disappeared after updating from the previous stable release.
A maintainer stated that the performance monitor widgets were decoupled in the latest release and can be added back through right-click Dock, Edit Dock.
PerformanceMonitorCommandsProvider creates separate Network, NetworkSpeed, and GPU band pages and maps them to NetworkIcon and GpuIcon.
The report includes a screenshot but the original reproduction steps do not establish that the icons are absent from Edit Dock or from the widget content itself.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the current Edit Dock flow to add the GPU and Network performance widgets back; only reopen code investigation if those widgets are absent from the editor or render without icons after being added.

fix_assessment.rationale: The available evidence indicates an intentional dock composition change and an existing user-facing recovery path, not a confirmed PowerToys code defect requiring a competing fix.

issue_context.summary: After updating to stable 0.101.2362, the reporter no longer sees GPU and Network icons in the Command Palette Performance Monitor dock. The latest maintainer response identifies the change as widget decoupling and points to Edit Dock for restoring the individual widgets, but the issue has not confirmed whether those widgets are missing from the editor as well.
known_information: The affected area is Command Palette Performance Monitor.
The reporter uses PowerToys 0.101.2362 stable on Windows 11 25H2.
The reporter identified the missing items as GPU and Network icons and said they were present in the prior stable update.
A screenshot is attached to the issue.
A maintainer provided the Edit Dock recovery steps on 2026-09-08.
The current provider source defines separate GPU and Network bands and their icon mappings.
inferences: The reporter may be comparing the previous default dock composition with the new decoupled widget composition rather than observing an icon resource failure.
If the GPU and Network entries are absent even from Edit Dock, the current explanation would be insufficient and a focused regression investigation would become appropriate.
issue_context.analysis: The latest public maintainer response directly addresses the symptom and is supported by the current provider structure: individual metric pages and dock bands are explicitly created, including GPU and Network. Because the report does not say whether the entries are available in Edit Dock, the safest classification is handled-by-current-UX rather than a speculative code design.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body and all five comments, including the reporter's clarification and the maintainer's current Edit Dock guidance.
Reviewed PerformanceMonitorCommandsProvider.cs: SetEnabledState creates separate network, network-speed, GPU, disk, and battery pages; GetBandIcon maps Network to NetworkIcon and GPU to GpuIcon.
Reviewed recent Performance Monitor history, including the August 2026 change reducing default perfmon band items and the dock activation lifecycle fix.
Searched related Performance Monitor issues; no duplicate specifically showing a missing icon resource was identified.

actions.label: Explain Edit Dock recovery
actions.note: Draft a maintainer response that records the current behavior and gives the documented recovery path.

comment.body: The latest Command Palette release decoupled the Performance Monitor widgets, so GPU and Network are no longer necessarily present in the default dock layout. Please right-click the dock, choose **Edit Dock**, and add the GPU and Network widgets back. If either widget is missing from the Edit Dock list, or appears without its icon after being added, please report that specific behavior so it can be investigated as a separate regression.
